cases.notes: Two competencies carried by measured outcomes on a ward, and a third claimed without a figure. Nursing evidence is counted in doses, shifts and audits, not in deploys.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a time you protected patient safety.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: On a night shift I raised a patient safety concern when the ward was 2 nurses short. The charge nurse backed me and we moved two admissions to the bay next door.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: What happened after that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The safety huddle I started now runs every 12 hours. It takes ten minutes and everyone on the bay is expected to be there.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about handover.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I redesigned the clinical handover sheet and missed medication doses fell from 7 a month to 1. The new sheet is one side of paper and nobody has to remember what goes on it.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Was that checked?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The handover audit covered 30 shifts and found no gaps. We ran it over a full rota so it was not just the quiet nights.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How do you handle a patient who is deteriorating?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I follow the escalation ladder every time but I have not counted them. It is second nature now rather than something I think about.

evidence.quote_contains: I raised a patient safety concern when the ward was 2 nurses short
The safety huddle I started now runs every 12 hours
I redesigned the clinical handover sheet
I follow the escalation ladder every time

variants.why: The same shift described by somebody who thinks aloud. Nothing about the evidence changed, so nothing about the judgement may.

cases.notes: A newly qualified nurse with one real example, one honest gap and one topic never reached. Thin evidence from a short career must read as thin evidence, never as a weak nurse.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about patient safety in your practice.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I raised one patient safety concern about a 3 day gap in the drug chart. My mentor took it from there and I did not follow it up.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about a clinical handover you led.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I do not know that I have a good clinical handover example. Most of mine were routine and I would rather not stretch one into something it was not.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: And escalation?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That did not come up in my last role. I was on a short rotation and the ward was quiet for most of it.

evidence.quote_contains: I raised one patient safety concern about a 3 day gap
I do not know that I have a good clinical handover example

cases.notes: A genuine conflict about the same caseload, plus escalation evidence alongside it, so the contradiction is not the only thing in the transcript.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: How many beds did you cover?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I covered 24 beds on that ward every shift. It was the busiest place I have worked and I would go back tomorrow.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Say a bit more about the ward.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: It was 30 beds on the ward and I covered all of them. Nobody else was allocated to that side of the corridor.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Tell me about escalating a deteriorating patient.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I called the escalation line twice in one night and both patients went to 4 hourly observations. The registrar came down inside ten minutes each time.

turns.speaker: interviewer
turns.text: Did anything change because of that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The escalation policy I wrote is now used across 3 wards. It went through the practice educator before it was adopted.

evidence.quote_contains: I called the escalation line twice in one night
The escalation policy I wrote is now used across 3 wards
both patients went to 4 hourly observations

contradictions.why: Twenty four beds every shift and thirty beds covered in full cannot both describe the same allocation.

known_limitations: The escalation sentence also earns a patient safety span, because evidence-1 matches competency tokens as substrings and patients contains patient. The link is coarse but the quote is honest, and a reviewer can see exactly which words produced it.

cases.notes: The candidate never spoke. Nothing here is a judgement about them: there is no answer to read, which is a fact about the session and not about the nurse.
